topic: Large Language Models for Automated Code Review: Techniques, Benchmarks, and Industrial Deployment

per_sentence.text: Pornprasit and Tantithamthavorn (2024) note that large language models (LLMs)—large deep learning models based on the transformer architecture—have been increasingly proposed for code review automation.

judge.rationale: The abstract explicitly states that the rapid evolution of LLMs has sparked significant interest in using them for code review automation, directly supporting the claim that LLMs have been increasingly proposed for this purpose.

per_sentence.text: Paul et al. (2023) describe DeepFix, which employed a neural network with an attention mechanism to predict fixes for common errors in C programs, and CoCoNut, which introduced the FConv architecture for automatic code repair, addressing limitations of prior neural machine translation methods.

judge.rationale: The cited evidence discusses PLBART, CodeT5, Codex, and GPT-3.5-Turbo for program repair but never mentions DeepFix, attention mechanisms, CoCoNut, or the FConv architecture, so it provides no support for the specific claim.

per_sentence.text: Building on these foundations, Paul et al. (2023) explored the use of different pre-trained models and LLMs to repair code based on code reviews, illustrating the evolution from task-specific neural architectures to general-purpose language models in software engineering.

judge.rationale: The evidence shows that Paul et al. (2023) explored pre-trained models and LLMs for code repair based on code reviews, but it does not explicitly illustrate an evolution from task-specific neural architectures to general-purpose language models in software engineering.

per_sentence.text: In the related domain of automated program repair, Paul et al. (2023) highlight earlier neural methods that paved the way for current LLM-based techniques.

judge.rationale: The abstract explicitly states that the authors applied PLBART and CodeT5 (pre-trained models) and performed prompt engineering with Codex and GPT-3.5-Turbo (LLMs) to repair code using datasets containing code review and subsequent code changes.
